decisions.rationale: The afternoon return choice can be naturally reaffirmed. Allowing near-afternoon departures when true afternoon options are limited or unattractive adds a reusable tradeoff rule beyond presenting afternoon options first; an explicit trip-specific timing request is a valid override.

Choosing nonstop naturally supports the policy. Calling it a preference rather than an absolute requirement only restates the existing prioritize-first default, while accepting one stop when no suitable nonstop exists permits a trip-specific override.

Including or favoring a comparable Delta option naturally supports the policy. The soft, nonexclusive characterization is already encoded in the preference and default action; Delta being unavailable or materially worse supports a current-trip carrier override.

Selecting the cheapest option from an acceptable shortlist naturally supports the policy. Not allowing price to override required constraints repeats the scope's acceptable-shortlist qualification, while choosing a costlier itinerary because the cheapest violates a must-have is a valid trip-specific exception.

Choosing a hotel with a pool and fitness facility, with a hot tub as a tiebreaker, naturally supports the policy. The core-versus-soft amenity distinction is already present in the default action, and the non-inference warnings add no concrete alternative behavior; relaxing amenities for current constraints is a valid exception.

Reaffirming the applicable rating floor naturally supports the policy. Restricting a threshold to the rating metric actually under discussion, without conflating class and review metrics, is a reusable scope rule with behavior beyond merely applying the numeric floor; a newly stated threshold or permission to relax it is a current-trip override.

Choosing a beach hotel within walking distance naturally supports the policy. The walking-distance threshold is already stated in the preference, default, and scope, so the alleged boundary only repeats it; a different location priority for the current trip is a valid override.

Selecting an afternoon departure naturally supports the policy. Excluding legs with an explicitly requested different period repeats the scope qualifier and functions as a current-trip exception, not an additional reusable boundary.

Choosing a connecting itinerary with at most one short layover naturally supports the policy. Limiting the rule to connecting itineraries repeats the condition and scope, and the warning against inferring a nonstop preference adds no alternative action; explicit stop requirements are valid trip-specific overrides.

Including United among suitable carrier options naturally supports the policy. Not ranking it above other carriers is already encoded by its acceptable-but-not-uniquely-favored status, while exclusion or material itinerary disadvantages can justify a current-trip alternative.

Requesting a window seat naturally supports the policy. Deferring the request until check-in when seat selection is unavailable is execution fallback rather than a separately testable boundary, and using another seat when no acceptable window is available or a different arrangement is requested is a valid exception.

Choosing a queen bed for the shared room naturally supports the policy. The per-room warning restates the existing shared-one-room scope and supplies no concrete reusable alternative action; an explicit separate-bed or other room-specific arrangement is a valid trip override.

Choosing a room with both a coffee maker and mini-fridge naturally supports the policy. The instruction not to infer unrelated amenities, destinations, dates, or prices is only a non-inference warning and provides no independently testable alternative behavior; relaxing either amenity for an otherwise suitable current stay is a valid exception.
